clue.text: Use key to unlock secret passage

definitions.text: Use key to unlock secret passage

parts.words: Use key to unlock secret passage
parts.note: reads like finding a hidden tunnel with a key, but the key is a code key and the passage is a coded piece of text

explanation.surface: Someone opens a hidden tunnel with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' means a stretch of writing, not a corridor, and the 'key' is the one that cracks a cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out coded text with its key is to turn a cipher back into plain language.

clue.text: Separate from the cad

indicators.note: from is read as made from, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep away from a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is the weak anagram signal, meaning made from the letters THECAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or disconnect something is to part it from the rest.

clue.text: Rowing boat said to be for sale in the Levant

annotationWithheld.why: Rowing boat said to be for sale in the Levant (6): CAIQUE is a Levantine skiff, but no word said aloud for 'for sale' sounds like it, so 'said to be for sale' has no parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Rowing boat said to be for sale in the Levant

clue.text: Simple standard made from kepi on a pole

indicators.note: made from says the cap's letters are reworked into a new word

parts.note: a staff is a pole or rod

explanation.surface: A plain flag fashioned from a soldier's cap on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: A kepi is a French military cap. 'Simple' points to the phrase 'plain as a pikestaff'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden shaft carrying a spearhead is a standard pole, and the phrase 'plain as a pikestaff' makes it a byword for something simple.

clue.text: This is no time for a morning tea-break — it's very late

definitions.text: This is no time for a morning tea-break — it's very late

parts.words: This is no time for a morning tea-break — it's very late
parts.note: the mid-morning break is 11 o'clock, elevenses, but the phrase for that hour means the last possible moment

explanation.surface: A boss refuses a mid-morning cuppa because work is running behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack at about 11 a.m.; the clue plays on the phrase meaning the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the last possible moment, when it is almost too late to act.

clue.text: Cut out to cheat

explanation.surface: A plain instruction to cut out cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver's tool cuts out shapes in wood or stone; as a slang verb it means swindle someone.

clue.text: Utter bliss without end

indicators.note: without end says the final letter of the word for bliss is dropped

parts.note: heaven means perfect happiness

explanation.surface: A phrase for complete, unending happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning total; it is the verb, as in heaving a sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out a sigh or groan with effort is to let it out, to voice it.

clue.text: Chinese study shows long love is unusual, and says why

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of long, the love letter and is are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: says tells us the word why is heard, giving the letter with that sound

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

explanation.surface: Studying China shows that lasting love is rare, and explains the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges LONGOIS into SINOLOG; 'says' turns 'why' into its sound-alike letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic discipline devoted to China's language, history and culture is Chinese studies.

clue.text: No call for oaths in such inscriptions, said Johnson

definitions.text: No call for oaths in such inscriptions, said Johnson

parts.words: No call for oaths in such inscriptions, said Johnson
parts.note: Samuel Johnson remarked that in carved memorial inscriptions a man is not upon oath, so praise need not be strictly true

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's remark that epitaphs need not be sworn truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson's dictum, recorded by Boswell, was that in inscriptions of this kind a man is not upon oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraved in stone, as on monuments, inscriptions are carved in the stonecutter's style.

clue.text: Dull part of the class — very solid

parts.note: thick means stupid or dull-witted
a set is a group of pupils of similar ability within a school year

explanation.surface: A teacher grumbles that the slow stream of the class is very dense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky, heavily built body or object is sturdy and solid.

clue.text: Plant for pet to bite

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
nip means to bite lightly

explanation.surface: A herb kept for the pet to chew on.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-family herb whose scent excites cats is a plant.

clue.text: Broadway's rating of musical is very thin indeed

parts.note: Hair is the rock musical; 'of' gives it the possessive
the measure of how broad a way is would be its width

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict on a Broadway show is that it is very slight.
explanation.walkthrough: A pun: a show called Hair is measured by its width on a broad way, giving the phrase for a tiny margin.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an extremely narrow margin, as slim as a single strand.

clue.text: Friends, the stupid fellow's gone soft

indicators.note: gone says a letter has left the word for the stupid fellow

parts.note: a chump is a fool; with the possessive 's it gives the plural-looking form
P stands for piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their foolish pal has grown soft in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'fellow's' supplies an S, so CHUMP'S loses its P, the piano or soft letter, leaving the word for pals.
explanation.definitionFit: Close companions, in informal British speech, are mates or pals.

clue.text: Put a gloss on title the Spanish were the first to hold

indicators.note: to hold says the Spanish article wraps round the word for title

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a name is what a thing is titled
led means were in front, were first

explanation.surface: The Spanish were the first to hold a certain title, burnishing their reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' looks like a noun being glossed; it is the name held inside the Spanish article, and 'were the first' is a verb phrase for leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Coated with a glassy glaze, a surface has been given a glossy finish.

clue.text: One who appears, in opera, to control the diva

parts.note: to master is to control
a diva is a leading female singer

explanation.surface: A performer turns up in an opera determined to dominate its leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg is about guild members of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a medieval German guild of poets and musicians features in Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Lack of point in a public service, perhaps

parts.note: a utility is a public service such as gas, water or electricity

explanation.surface: A complaint that a public service is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a public service as an example of a utility.
explanation.definitionFit: Uselessness means having no purpose, no point.

clue.text: Bits of paper left behind after a union celebration

definitions.text: Bits of paper left behind after a union celebration

parts.words: Bits of paper left behind after a union celebration
parts.note: union suggests a trade union party, but it is a marriage, where guests throw scraps of coloured paper

explanation.surface: Litter left after a trade union party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' means a wedding, not a labour union.
explanation.definitionFit: Small paper scraps thrown over newlyweds litter the ground after a wedding.

clue.text: Guidance here on the cheapest way to travel

explanation.surface: Advice on how to travel as cheaply as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering a vessel is guiding it, and the lowest-fare section of a passenger ship was its cheapest accommodation.

clue.text: Arriving thus unexpectedly, owing to fine weather

explanation.surface: Someone turns up by surprise, thanks to a sunny day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without warning; taken literally it means coming from a clear sky, which fine weather gives.

clue.text: Grilled piece of meat without ado in charcoal

indicators.note: without says the word ado is taken away from the grilled dish

parts.note: a carbonado is a piece of meat scored and grilled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A steak barbecued over charcoal with no fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Carbonado is an old word for meat grilled on coals; Shakespeare uses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is almost pure elemental carbon, the chemical element in it.

clue.text: One old-fashioned simpleton

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped, so the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: An outdated name for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' looks like one adjective; 'old' is fodder and 'fashioned' the anagram signal on ONEOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, dated slang word for a silly or foolish person, a dimwit.

clue.text: No charge for bingo in this pub

parts.note: free means costing nothing
house, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo

explanation.surface: A pub that lets its customers play bingo for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a pub not tied to one brewery, free to sell any beer, has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A British tavern not owned by a brewery is called this, so it is a kind of pub.

clue.text: Express surprise at ring of light round lake

indicators.note: round says the ring of light goes around the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light, as round a saint's head
L is a standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a halo seen over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a cry of greeting or surprise, said when startled.

clue.text: Maiden appears in ancient, idealised picture

annotationWithheld.why: Maiden appears in ancient, idealised picture (5): M + AGO account for four letters, but no clue word gives the leading I
annotationWithheld.clue: Maiden appears in ancient, idealised picture

clue.text: It sounds natural for Walpole to make him follow Mr Perrin

definitions.text: It sounds natural for Walpole to make him follow Mr Perrin

parts.words: It sounds natural for Walpole to make him follow Mr Perrin
parts.note: Hugh Walpole's novel is titled after two schoolmasters, this one named second, after Perrin; his surname sounds like a verb for coming along behind

explanation.surface: A remark that the novelist Walpole naturally put this character second in his title.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Walpole's 1911 novel 'Mr Perrin and Mr Traill' names two rival schoolmasters; the second name sounds like a word meaning follow, so it is natural for him to come after Perrin.
explanation.definitionFit: The younger master in Walpole's school novel bears this surname, the man who comes after Perrin in its title.

clue.text: Made up words, as Babel did when confounded

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: The builders of Babel invented speech when God confused their languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When confounded' scrambles BABELDID; the surface recalls the confusion of tongues at Babel.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised speech without a script is speech made up on the spot.

clue.text: Manufacturer of solid-state coolers

parts.note: sounds like an electronics firm, but solid-state means frozen water and the coolers are cubes for drinks

explanation.surface: A firm that makes electronic cooling units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid-state' suggests transistors; here it is water in its solid state, made in a freezer compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator compartment makes frozen cubes that chill drinks, so it produces coolers of solid water.

clue.text: A Red Indian (he could turn into a red pepper!)

indicators.note: says that swapping two letters for one word turns the tribe's name into the spice, so working backwards the spice gives the name

parts.note: cayenne is a hot red pepper

explanation.surface: A Native American is joked to be capable of becoming a hot spice.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: in CAYENNE put HE where the A is and you get the tribe. 'Red Indian' is an old term for a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: A Plains people of North America are a Native American nation, called in old usage a Red Indian tribe.
